The Andai dance of the Horqin Mongols is on China's national list of intangible heritage.

q.q: Which sandy land surrounds Tongliao?

ne-pp-1159149875.t: A green oasis between the desert and the Karakoram
ne-pp-1159149875.s: Shache, long known as Yarkand, is a vast green oasis on the western edge of the Taklamakan: fields and rows of poplars fan out from the Yarkand River across the pale desert. The river comes down from the Karakoram, near K2, and snowy ranges line the southern horizon. From 1514 this was the capital of the Yarkand Khanate, a centre of Uyghur music and learning.
ne-pp-1159149875.w: A huge fan of green fields and tree lines on pale desert, fed by a braided river, high mountains to the south.
f: Queen Amannisa Khan, a 16th-century poet and musician, is credited with collecting the Uyghur Twelve Muqam.
The Uyghur Muqam is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
The tombs of the Yarkand khans stand beside the Altun Mosque in the old town.

q.q: Which river waters the oasis of Shache?

Q151958.t: A lakeside tower that gave China a motto
Q151958.s: Dongting Lake spreads west of Yueyang, and its size depends on the season: a vast sheet of water in summer, a web of channels and green meadows in winter. Just north of the city the lake drains into the Yangtze. On the old city wall stands Yueyang Tower, subject of Fan Zhongyan's essay of 1046, whose lines on duty every Chinese schoolchild learns.
Q151958.w: A city on the east shore of a huge lake, which drains into the wide Yangtze just to the north.
f: Fan Zhongyan wrote that officials should be first to worry and last to rejoice.
Junshan Island, in the lake, grows Junshan Yinzhen, a rare yellow tea.
Dongting is China's second-largest freshwater lake, after Poyang.

q.q: Which lake does Yueyang Tower overlook?

Q59107.t: Red cliffs that gave a whole landscape its name
Q59107.s: Two rivers, the Zhen and the Wu, meet at Shaoguan to form the Bei, the “north river” that flows south to Guangzhou. North-east of the city rises Danxia Shan, a cluster of red sandstone cliffs and towers so distinctive that geologists named a whole type of landscape, danxia, after it. For centuries travellers crossed the mountains here on the main road between central China and the south.
Q59107.w: A city at a river junction in the hills of northern Guangdong, with red rocky peaks to the north-east.
f: Danxia Shan is part of the “China Danxia” UNESCO World Heritage site, listed in 2010.
Nanhua Temple keeps what is said to be the preserved body of Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of Chan Buddhism.
The Meiling Pass, north-east of the city, was for centuries the main gateway into Guangdong from the north.

q.q: Which landscape type is named after a mountain near Shaoguan?

Q128849.t: An Olympic city in a ring of snowy Alps
Q128849.s: In winter, snow-capped peaks of the Japanese Alps rise on every side of Nagano's broad valley, where a tributary joins the Chikuma, the upper Shinano. The city grew up around Zenkō-ji, a temple said to date from the 7th century that still draws millions of pilgrims. In 1998 Nagano hosted the Winter Olympics.
Q128849.w: A city in a wide, flat valley ringed by high mountains, snowy in winter, where two rivers join.
f: The Shinano, which flows past the city as the Chikuma, is Japan's longest river, about 367 km.
At Jigokudani, north-east of the city, wild Japanese macaques bathe in hot springs in winter.
Zenkō-ji's main hall, rebuilt in 1707, is one of Japan's largest wooden buildings.

q.q: In which year did Nagano host the Winter Olympics?

Q866021.t: The green valley of the Ili, Xinjiang's garden
Q866021.s: Westerly winds carry rain into the Ili valley, making it the greenest corner of Xinjiang: fields, orchards and rows of poplars fill the valley floor between snowy ranges of the Tian Shan. Yining, long known in Russian as Kulja, sits on the north bank of the Ili River, which flows west into Kazakhstan. In June the fields west of the city turn purple with lavender.
Q866021.w: A green city on the north bank of a wide river in a broad valley, with snow-capped ranges to the north and south.
f: The Ili River ends in Lake Balkhash, far away in Kazakhstan.
Sayram Lake, an alpine lake at about 2,070 m, lies in the mountains to the north.
Under an 1851 treaty, a Russian consulate and trading post opened in Kulja.

q.q: Where does the Ili River, flowing past Kulja, end?

Q249007.t: Home of the bronze horse that treads on a swallow
Q249007.s: Wuwei is an oasis at the eastern end of the Hexi Corridor, the long strip between the snowy Qilian Mountains and the Tengger Desert that carried the Silk Road west. Its irrigated green stands out sharply against the yellow sand to the north-east. In 1969 a Han tomb here yielded the bronze “Flying Horse of Gansu”, galloping on a swallow's back — now an emblem of Chinese tourism.
Q249007.w: A green oasis city on a strip of land between snow-capped mountains to the south and desert to the north-east.
f: As Liangzhou, Wuwei was home for about 17 years to the monk Kumarajiva, a great translator of Buddhist texts.
The Flying Horse of Gansu is only about 34 cm tall.
The Tengger Desert presses against the oasis from the north-east.

q.q: What does the famous bronze horse from Wuwei tread on?

Q571652.t: Where a green river meets a brown one
Q571652.s: At Wuzhou the clear green Gui River meets the muddier Xun, and for a while the two colours run side by side before blending into the Xi, the West River, which carries on to Guangzhou and the sea. The city is a gateway between Guangxi and Guangdong. Its old arcaded shophouses have doors on their upper floors, used whenever the rivers flooded the streets.
Q571652.w: A hilly city where two rivers of different colours join, the combined river flowing on east towards Guangdong.
f: Wuzhou is famous for guilinggao, a dark, bitter herbal jelly.
In floods, boats were tied to rings on the arcade pillars, and people came and went through the upper doors.
The Xi carries more water than any other branch of the Pearl River system.

q.q: Which river begins where the Gui and Xun meet at Wuzhou?

Q224603.t: The “moon city”, and a launch pad to the Moon
Q224603.s: Clear, dry skies over the Anning valley earned Xichang the nickname “moon city”, and the same skies made it a launch site: up the valley to the north, the Xichang Satellite Launch Centre sent China's first probes to the Moon. The city lies at about 1,500 m beside Qionghai, a large freshwater lake, among the mountains of the Liangshan Yi region.
Q224603.w: A city in a long mountain valley beside a large lake, with high ridges on both sides.
f: The Chang'e 1 lunar probe lifted off from the Xichang launch centre in 2007.
The Yi people celebrate their Torch Festival here every summer.
Qionghai Lake, about 30 km² in area, lies just south-east of the city.

q.q: What is Xichang nicknamed for its clear skies?

Q200251.t: An original castle and the home of a Meiji hero
Q200251.s: Kōchi faces the Pacific from the south coast of Shikoku, on a small plain between forested mountains and the long, narrow Urado Bay. Above its centre rises one of the few Japanese castles to keep its original keep. Sakamoto Ryōma, a hero of the Meiji Restoration, was born here in 1836, and every August the city dances the Yosakoi, a festival it invented.
Q200251.w: A city on a small plain on Shikoku's south coast, between forested mountains and a narrow bay opening to the Pacific.
f: Kōchi Castle is one of only twelve Japanese castles whose original keep survives.
The Yosakoi dance festival began in Kōchi in 1954 and has spread all over Japan.
About 84% of Kōchi prefecture is forest, the highest share in Japan.

q.q: Which dance festival was born in Kōchi?

Q109374.t: A deep east-coast bay sheltered by a sandspit
Q109374.s: Wonsan sits at the head of a deep bay on Korea's east coast, sheltered by a long sandy spit and scattered with small islands, with steep mountains close behind. In 1880 it became one of Korea's first ports open to foreign trade. South-east along the coast rise the Kumgang Mountains, the “Diamond Mountains”, celebrated for centuries for their granite pinnacles.
Q109374.w: A port at the head of a deep bay on the east coast, with a long sandy spit, small islands and mountains behind.
f: Tradition says the Kumgang Mountains have 12,000 peaks.
The Japanese knew Wonsan as Gensan.
Thanks to the sea, winters here are milder than in Pyongyang.

q.q: Which famous mountains lie south-east of Wonsan?

Q204308.t: Palms, surf and the legend of Japan's first emperor
Q204308.s: Miyazaki basks on the sunny Pacific coast of Kyushu: a long, straight shore lined with pines, palm-lined avenues and surf. South of the city, rock ridges stripe the shore around little Aoshima island like a giant washboard. According to legend, Jimmu, the first emperor, set out from this coast, then called Hyūga, on his journey east to found the Japanese state.
Q204308.w: A city on a long, straight Pacific shore of eastern Kyushu, with green hills inland and rocky reefs to the south.
f: The “Devil's Washboard” ridges at Aoshima are tilted layers of sandstone and mudstone.
Miyazaki's greenhouse mangoes are among the most expensive fruits in Japan.
Udo Shrine, south of the city, is built inside a sea cave in the cliffs.

q.q: What are the rock ridges around Aoshima called?

Q26418.t: A city on a sandy neck, with a mountain at the end
Q26418.s: Hakodate has one of Japan's most recognisable shapes: a narrow neck of land between two bays, pinched like an hourglass, with the dark hump of Mount Hakodate at its tip. The mountain was once an island; sand joined it to Hokkaido. At night the neck glows between two black seas, and in summer the lights of squid boats dot the Tsugaru Strait.
Q26418.w: An hourglass-shaped city on a narrow isthmus between two bays, ending in a rounded, wooded mountain at Hokkaido's southern tip.
f: Hakodate was one of the first Japanese ports opened to foreign trade, in 1859.
Goryōkaku, a star-shaped Western-style fort, was completed here in 1864.
Mount Hakodate is 334 m high.

q.q: What shape is Hakodate's Goryōkaku fort?

Q156243.t: Facing its Chinese neighbour across the Yalu
Q156243.s: Two cities face each other across the Yalu near its mouth: Sinuiju on the south bank and the Chinese city of Dandong opposite, with long, low islands of silt splitting the river between them. The Yalu rises near Paektu Mountain and runs for almost 800 km to the Yellow Sea. On Wihwa Island in 1388, the general Yi Seong-gye turned his army back — a step towards founding the Joseon dynasty.
Q156243.w: A flat city on the south bank of a wide river near its mouth, with long islands in the river and another city opposite.
f: Sinuiju grew up in the early 20th century, after the railway from Seoul reached the Yalu.
Wide mudflats spread where the Yalu enters the Yellow Sea.
In Korean the Yalu is called the Amnok.

q.q: Which river separates Sinuiju from Dandong?

Q1000383.t: The “red city” at the foot of the Greater Khingan
Q1000383.s: A temple to Genghis Khan crowns a hill above Ulan Hot, and the city's name is Mongolian for “red city”. It lies on the Tao'er River where the forested Greater Khingan range gives way to open plain, with farmland to the south-east and grassland and forest to the north-west. In 1947 Ulan Hot became the first capital of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
Q1000383.w: A city on a river where the forested hills of the Greater Khingan meet open plain, with farmland to the south-east.
f: The Arxan volcanic area, with crater lakes and hot springs, lies in the Greater Khingan to the north-west.
The Tao'er River flows out of the Greater Khingan past the city towards the Nen River.
The Genghis Khan temple on the hill was built in the 1940s.

q.q: What does the name Ulan Hot mean?

Q986724.t: A frontier town in a sea of Hulunbuir grass
Q986724.s: Around Hailar the steppe rolls to the horizon, and the Hailar River traces looping meanders across it, edged with willows and oxbow lakes. This is the Hulunbuir grassland, one of China's finest, home to Mongol and Ewenki herders. The town began as a Qing garrison in 1734 and grew after the Chinese Eastern Railway arrived in the early 1900s. Winters here are long and bitterly cold.
Q986724.w: A city on a river that coils across wide, open steppe, with oxbow lakes and low hills around.
f: Hulun Lake, one of China's largest lakes, lies to the south-west.
January temperatures in Hailar average around −25 °C.
The railway runs on west from here to Manzhouli on the Russian border.

q.q: Which grassland surrounds Hailar?

Q197402.t: Rainbow hills on the Silk Road
Q197402.s: Zhangye is an oasis in the Hexi Corridor, watered by the Hei River coming down from the snowy Qilian Mountains to the south. West of the city, eroded sandstone hills are striped in red, orange, yellow and white — the famous “rainbow mountains” of the Danxia landform. In town, a temple founded in 1098 holds a reclining Buddha about 35 m long. Marco Polo stayed here for about a year.
Q197402.w: A green oasis in a long corridor between snowy mountains to the south and bare desert hills to the north.
f: The Zhangye Danxia hills owe their stripes to layers of sandstone and siltstone rich in different minerals.
The Great Buddha Temple's reclining Buddha is one of the largest indoor reclining Buddhas in China.
The Hei River flows north from here into the desert, ending near the poplar forests of Ejin.

q.q: What did Marco Polo call Zhangye?

Q271917.t: Sea fog and cranes beside Japan's largest wetland
Q271917.s: In summer, sea fog often rolls in over Kushiro from the cold Pacific, wrapping the port in grey while inland lies in sunshine. North of the city spreads Kushiro Marsh, Japan's largest wetland, a vast flat expanse of reeds and meandering streams. Red-crowned cranes, reduced to a handful here a century ago, now number more than a thousand across eastern Hokkaido.
Q271917.w: A port city on the Pacific coast of eastern Hokkaido, with a huge, flat brown-green marsh stretching north.
f: Kushiro Marsh became Japan's first Ramsar wetland in 1980.
Kushiro is one of Japan's main fishing ports.
The lakes and volcanoes of Akan lie to the north.

q.q: Which birds made Kushiro Marsh famous?

ne-pp-1159149783.t: Mango valley of the Right River
ne-pp-1159149783.s: The city at this spot is Baise, in western Guangxi, on the Youjiang — the “Right River” — which flows east through a wide valley towards Nanning. The valley is warm enough for mangoes, and orchards cover its slopes. Most people here are Zhuang, China's largest minority. The Baise Basin is also famous for stone hand axes about 800,000 years old.
ne-pp-1159149783.w: A city in a long, warm river valley with orchard-covered slopes, ringed by green mountains in western Guangxi.
f: The Baise hand axes, dated in 2000, challenged the idea that early Asian toolmakers lagged behind Africa's.
The Youjiang and the Zuojiang, the “Left River”, meet near Nanning to form the Yong River.
Zhuang, the language of Guangxi's largest ethnic group, is widely spoken in the city.

q.q: Which ancient tools made the Baise Basin famous?

Q515712.t: A Great Wall frontier where the desert turned green
Q515712.s: Sand once drifted against Yulin's walls: the town stands where the Loess Plateau meets the Mu Us Desert, on the line of the Ming Great Wall. Then decades of planting turned much of the desert green with grass and trees. North of the city rises Zhenbeitai, one of the largest watchtowers of the Great Wall. Beneath it all lie rich fields of coal and gas.
Q515712.w: A city on a river between yellow loess hills to the south and a green-speckled sandy plain to the north.
f: The name means “elm forest”.
Yulin was one of the nine frontier garrisons of the Ming Great Wall.
Zhenbeitai was built in 1607.

q.q: Which desert borders Yulin?

Q814616.t: Black-soil prairie near five lava-dammed lakes
Q814616.s: Around Bei'an the land is flat and black: this is the heart of north-east China's black-soil belt, among the most fertile farmland in the world, laid out in vast rectangles of soybeans and corn. North-west of town rise the cones of Wudalianchi, volcanoes that erupted in 1719–1721 and dammed a river into five linked lakes. Winters here are long and fierce.
Q814616.w: A town amid vast rectangular fields on a flat plain, with small volcanic cones and lakes to the north-west.
f: Bei'an means “peace in the north”.
Wudalianchi's lava fields and mineral springs form a UNESCO Global Geopark.
Wudalianchi has 14 volcanoes; the youngest, Laoheishan and Huoshaoshan, grew in the eruptions of the 1720s.

q.q: What dammed the river to form the Wudalianchi lakes near Bei'an?

Q1016730.t: China's tin capital in the Yunnan mountains
Q1016730.s: Tin built Gejiu. The metal has been mined in these mountains of southern Yunnan for some two thousand years, and the city, squeezed into a narrow valley at about 1,700 m with a lake at its heart, became known as China's tin capital. In the early 20th century local merchants even built their own narrow-gauge railway to carry the ore down to the line to Vietnam.
Q1016730.w: A city squeezed into a narrow mountain valley with a small lake in its centre and hills scarred by old mines.
f: Gejiu's narrow-gauge railway had its rails just 600 mm apart.
Tin from Gejiu was shipped abroad through the Vietnamese port of Haiphong.
The Honghe Hani Rice Terraces, a UNESCO site, lie to the south beyond the Red River.

q.q: Which metal made Gejiu famous?

Q434924.t: A gold-mountain town on a river bound for the Arctic
Q434924.s: The river at Altay is bound for the Arctic. The town's Kelan River soon joins the Irtysh, which does something no other river in China does: it flows through Kazakhstan and Russia to the Arctic Ocean. Altay sits at the foot of the Altai Mountains in Xinjiang's far north; their name is usually linked to the Mongolic word for gold, and gold has been panned here for centuries.
Q434924.w: A town in a mountain valley where the forested slopes of the Altai meet dry steppe, with a river running south.
f: Altay promotes itself as a birthplace of skiing, citing ancient rock paintings of skiers.
Kanas Lake, a long glacial lake known for its changing colours, lies in the mountains to the north.
Snow lies here for months, and ski resorts dot the nearby slopes.

q.q: Which ocean does the Irtysh, near Altay, finally reach?

Q319114.t: Painted caves and singing dunes at the desert's edge
Q319114.s: Dunhuang is a green island in the desert: fields and poplars ring the town, and then the sand begins. To the south, the dunes of Mingsha Shan rise in sharp golden ridges around a small crescent-shaped lake. In a cliff south-east of town, the Mogao Caves hold nearly 500 grottoes painted over a thousand years, when this was the Silk Road's gateway into China.
Q319114.w: A small green oasis surrounded by desert, with high golden dunes immediately to the south.
f: A sealed library cave found in 1900 held the Diamond Sutra of 868, the oldest dated printed book.
The Mingsha dunes are said to “sing”: they hum when sand slides down their slopes.
The Mogao Caves have been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1987.

q.q: What is the Diamond Sutra from Dunhuang famous as?

Q604385.t: A mountain wall above the Yellow River
Q604385.s: The Yellow River runs north here between two worlds: on its west bank, the irrigated Ningxia plain and the bare, jagged wall of the Helan Mountains; to the east, the sands of the Ordos. Shizuishan, a town of coal and industry, takes its name from rocks that jut into the river like a beak. South of the city, at Sand Lake, dunes run straight down to reed-fringed water.
Q604385.w: A city on the west bank of the Yellow River, a dark mountain wall to the west and sandy desert across the river.
f: The name means “stone-beak hill”.
The Helan Mountains shelter the plain from the winds and sands of the Tengger Desert to the west.
Ningxia's irrigation canals, fed by the Yellow River, go back more than 2,000 years.

q.q: Which mountains rise west of Shizuishan?

Q858250.t: A salt-lake town on the road to Lhasa
Q858250.s: Poplars mark an oasis at about 2,800 m in the Qaidam Basin: Golmud, between salt flats to the north and the Kunlun Mountains to the south. North of town lies Qarhan, China's largest salt lake, where a road more than 30 km long is built on solid salt. From Golmud the railway to Lhasa climbs across the Tibetan Plateau, cresting at over 5,000 m.
Q858250.w: A town on a gravel plain between white salt flats to the north and high, snow-streaked mountains to the south.
f: The Qarhan salt flats produce much of China's potash fertiliser.
The railway from Golmud to Lhasa opened in 2006.
The Tanggula Pass on that line, at about 5,070 m, is the highest point on any railway in the world.

q.q: What is the “Salt Bridge” road near Golmud built on?

Q975264.t: Ancient capital of Jin in the Fen River valley
Q975264.s: In the broad Fen River valley of southern Shanxi, terraced loess hills step down to the plain where the Hui River joins the Fen. From 585 BC this was Xintian, capital of Jin, one of the great states of ancient China. Archaeologists here have found a vast bronze foundry and stone tablets inscribed in red with the oaths of Jin nobles.
Q975264.w: A town on a plain at a river junction, with terraced yellow loess hills stepping up on both sides.
f: The Houma Covenant Texts, found in 1965, are oaths written in red on stone and jade tablets.
The Jin bronze foundry yielded tens of thousands of fragments of clay moulds.
Houma is a railway junction of southern Shanxi.

q.q: Which ancient state had its capital at Houma?

Q504690.t: A rice port at the mouth of the Mogami
Q504690.s: The Mogami River reaches the Sea of Japan at Sakata after crossing the Shōnai Plain, one of Japan's great rice bowls — green in summer, gold in autumn, white in winter. Rice made the port rich, carried away by coastal trading ships. To the north-east rises Mount Chōkai, a 2,236 m volcano that often keeps its snow well into summer.
Q504690.w: A port city at a river mouth on the Sea of Japan, a wide flat rice plain inland and a big volcano to the north-east.
f: The Sankyo rice warehouses of 1893, shaded by zelkova trees, still stand by the river.
The Honma family of Sakata were once among Japan's richest landowners.
Homma Munehisa, an 18th-century rice trader from Sakata, is often credited with inventing candlestick charts.

q.q: Which river reaches the sea at Sakata?

Q1211183.t: Tibet's second city, higher than Mount Fuji
Q1211183.s: At about 3,840 m, Xigazê sits higher than the summit of Mount Fuji, in a wide valley where the Nyang River joins the Yarlung Tsangpo. Barley fields make green patches against bare brown mountains. Above the town spread the golden roofs of Tashilhunpo Monastery, founded in 1447. Far to the south, the region reaches all the way to the north face of Everest.
Q1211183.w: A town in a broad, flat valley of green fields where two rivers meet, ringed by bare brown mountains.
f: Tashilhunpo was founded in 1447 by Gendun Drup, later counted as the first Dalai Lama.
From here the Yarlung Tsangpo flows east, becoming the Brahmaputra in India.
Xigazê is the second-largest city in Tibet.

q.q: Which famous monastery stands in Xigazê?

Q318245.t: A steppe town on the Kherlen in Mongolia's far east
Q318245.s: Choibalsan lies on the Kherlen River in the far east of Mongolia, in an immense flat steppe that rolls to the horizon in every direction. These plains are home to vast herds of Mongolian gazelles. The Kherlen rises far to the west in the Khentii Mountains and flows on from here into China, ending in Hulun Lake. The town is the capital of Dornod province.
Q318245.w: A small town on a meandering river in an immense, flat, treeless steppe.
f: Before 1941 the town was called Bayan Tümen.
The Kherlen is more than 1,000 km long.
Mongolian gazelles here can migrate in herds tens of thousands strong.

q.q: Which river flows past Choibalsan?

Q731256.t: An oasis town in the shadow of the Mongolian Altai
Q731256.s: This is Khovd, the main town of western Mongolia's province of the same name: a green strip of fields along the Buyant River in a dry valley ringed by the ranges of the Mongolian Altai. It began in 1762 as a Qing fortress town, and traces of its walls remain. To the east lies the Great Lakes Depression, with the reedy Khar-Us Lake.
Q731256.w: A green oasis town on a river in a dry valley, mountains around it and a big reedy lake to the east.
f: Khovd's melons and watermelons, grown on irrigated fields by the river, are famous across Mongolia.
Khovd province is home to more ethnic groups than any other province of Mongolia.
The ruins of the Qing fortress are known as Sangiin Kherem.

q.q: Which river flows through Khovd?

Q822808.t: Gateway to the Gobi's dinosaur cliffs
Q822808.s: Dalanzadgad sits on a gravel plain of the Gobi as the capital of South Gobi province. To the west rise the Gurvan Saikhan mountains, the “three beauties”, where ice often lingers into summer in the narrow gorge of Yolyn Am. Some 100 km to the north-west lie the Flaming Cliffs of Bayanzag, where in 1923 an American expedition found the first dinosaur eggs recognised by science.
Q822808.w: A small town on a flat gravel desert plain, with a dark mountain range rising to the west.
f: At sunset Bayanzag's cliffs glow orange-red, which gave them their English name.
The expedition was led by Roy Chapman Andrews of the American Museum of Natural History.
The singing dunes of Khongoryn Els lie farther west, beyond the Gurvan Saikhan.

q.q: What was found at the Flaming Cliffs near Dalanzadgad in 1923?

ne-pp-1159149777.t: Ancient tombs on the edge of the Qaidam Basin
ne-pp-1159149777.s: Dulan county lies on the south-eastern edge of the Qaidam Basin in Qinghai, above 3,000 m, where dry gravel plains meet the bare ridges of the Kunlun. Irrigated fields and goji orchards make green strips along the streams. On the hills around Reshui stand hundreds of burial mounds from the 7th to 9th centuries, when first the Tuyuhun and then the Tibetan Empire ruled here.
ne-pp-1159149777.w: A small oasis town on a dry plain at the foot of bare mountains, with green strips of fields along the streams.
f: Silks found in the Reshui tombs show that Silk Road trade crossed this high country.
Goji berries from the Qaidam Basin, Dulan included, are sold all over China.
The highway from Xining to Golmud and Lhasa runs through the county.

q.q: Which basin does Dulan county border?
